reader.summary: 07-learning-from-the-numbers.html 8/10. A newcomer would follow the numbers easily, but would meet the word "estimate" in the last step before it is explained, and the advice on where to write the lesson down is vague.

history.summary: 07-learning-from-the-numbers.html 8/10. A newcomer would follow the numbers easily, but would meet the word "estimate" in the last step before it is explained, and the advice on where to write the lesson down is vague.
07-learning-from-the-numbers.html 7/10.

07-when-people-change.html 7/10. A newcomer would get stuck on the idea of channels: a quiz uses the channel count before the lesson explains what a channel is, and 'sponsor' appears without a definition.

07-looking-back-together.html 8/10. A reader who has finished the beginner lessons would follow this almost all the way; the snags are a few words the lesson leans on from earlier lessons, such as "owned", "stand-up" and "iteration", and the difference between points and percent.
07-learning-from-risks.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly struggle in Step 2, where one example reuses the 3 from Step 1 and the idea of a surprise is only defined inside the example.

07-learning-from-risks.html 7/10. A newcomer would most likely get stuck on the project terms risk register, reserve and response, which the lesson uses before explaining them, and on a pair of example numbers that do not agree with each other.
07-judging-an-ai-tool.html 8/10. A newcomer would follow the four questions easily, but would struggle to see where the 90% bar comes from and what "accuracy" means in the checking step.
07-judging-an-ai-tool.html 7/10.

24-supplier-management.html 8/10. A newcomer would most likely stumble at the subtraction of the supplier's hours from the customer promise, because the lesson never says the two parts happen one after another, and the last check asks for a percentage share that was never taught.

07-reviewing-ai-use.html 8/10. A newcomer would mostly be stuck on the numbers: the lesson says 15% is high enough to act on but never says what counts as high, and it does not explain how percentage points differ from a percent change.
10-standing-instructions.html 8/10. A newcomer would struggle most with how to judge whether an answer followed a rule, and which rule to fix when it did not.
09-testing-a-prompt.html 8/10.
